cards.q: Adrenal structure that makes corticosteroids
cards.a: Adrenal cortex

cards.q: Carbon count and core ring system of corticoids
cards.a: 21 carbons; cyclopentanoperhydrophenanthrene (steroid) nucleus

cards.q: Precursor from which all adrenal steroids are made
cards.a: Cholesterol

cards.q: Pituitary hormone that drives adrenal steroid synthesis
cards.a: ACTH (frees cholesterol, induces steroidogenic enzymes)

cards.q: Why corticosteroid release follows synthesis rate
cards.a: Cortex stores very little hormone; release equals biosynthesis

cards.q: Who showed corticosteroid benefit in rheumatoid arthritis, and when
cards.a: Hench, 1949, with cortisone

cards.q: Collective name for natural and synthetic gluco- and mineralocorticoids
cards.a: Corticosteroids (corticoids)

cards.q: Principal mineralocorticoid and its renal effect
cards.a: Aldosterone: increases Na+ reabsorption in distal convoluted tubule

cards.q: Ions excreted in exchange when aldosterone retains Na+
cards.a: K+ and H+

cards.q: Mechanism of aldosterone action on tubular cells
cards.a: Gene-mediated protein synthesis (aldosterone-induced proteins)

cards.q: Major aldosterone-induced protein in renal tubule
cards.a: Basolateral Na+/K+ ATPase

cards.q: Main adverse effect of excess mineralocorticoid action
cards.a: Fluid retention and hypertension

cards.q: Glucocorticoid effect on liver glycogen
cards.a: Glycogen deposition (basis of the assay); induces hepatic glycogen synthase

cards.q: Glucocorticoid effect on peripheral glucose use
cards.a: Inhibits glucose utilisation, causing insulin resistance and hyperglycaemia

cards.q: Glucocorticoid effect on fat metabolism
cards.a: Permissive lipolysis; body fat redistributed (lost from limbs, gained centrally)

cards.q: Enzyme that makes active hydrocortisone in target tissue
cards.a: 11-beta-HSD1 (cortisone to hydrocortisone)

cards.q: Enzyme that inactivates hydrocortisone in kidney, colon, salivary gland
cards.a: 11-beta-HSD2 (hydrocortisone to cortisone)

cards.q: Effect of glucocorticoids on calcium balance
cards.a: Reduce intestinal Ca2+ absorption, raise renal Ca2+ loss; negative balance

cards.q: Bones most affected by glucocorticoid bone loss
cards.a: Spongy bones (vertebrae, ribs, pelvis)

cards.q: Water handling by glucocorticoids versus aldosterone
cards.a: Glucocorticoids maintain GFR and water excretion; aldosterone does not

cards.q: Cardiovascular effect of glucocorticoids
cards.a: Maintain arteriolar tone, capillary integrity and myocardial contractility

cards.q: Permissive vascular role of glucocorticoids
cards.a: Needed for pressor action of adrenaline and angiotensin

cards.q: Muscle effect of excess glucocorticoid
cards.a: Muscle wasting and proximal myopathy

cards.q: Mood effect of supraphysiological glucocorticoid doses
cards.a: Mild euphoria; may progress to mania or depression

cards.q: Seizure effect of high-dose glucocorticoids
cards.a: Lower the seizure threshold

cards.q: Gastric effect of glucocorticoids
cards.a: Increase acid and pepsin secretion; aggravate peptic ulcer

cards.q: Fetal organ matured by glucocorticoids near term
cards.a: Lungs: surfactant production and structural maturation

cards.q: Lymphoid cell most sensitive to glucocorticoid lysis
cards.a: T cells (more than B cells)

cards.q: Blood cell counts that rise on glucocorticoids
cards.a: Neutrophils, RBCs and platelets

cards.q: Blood cell counts that fall on glucocorticoids
cards.a: Lymphocytes, eosinophils, basophils (sequestration, not destruction)

cards.q: Time for blood counts to return after a glucocorticoid dose
cards.a: About 24 hours

cards.q: Protein induced by glucocorticoids that blocks phospholipase A2
cards.a: Annexins (lipocortins)

cards.q: Inflammatory enzyme negatively regulated by glucocorticoids
cards.a: COX-2 (inducible prostaglandin production)

cards.q: Basic anti-inflammatory mechanism of glucocorticoids
cards.a: Reduce recruitment of inflammatory cells and PG, LT and PAF production

cards.q: Immune function most suppressed by glucocorticoids
cards.a: Cell-mediated immunity (T cells); antibody production largely spared

cards.q: Cytokines whose production is reduced by glucocorticoids
cards.a: IL-1, IL-2, IL-3, IL-6, TNF, GM-CSF and interferon

cards.q: Endothelial adhesion molecules reduced by glucocorticoids
cards.a: ELAM-1 and ICAM-1

cards.q: Intracellular receptor type for glucocorticoids
cards.a: Cytoplasmic glucocorticoid receptor (GR); binds glucocorticoid response elements

cards.q: Approximate size of the glucocorticoid receptor
cards.a: About 800 amino acids

cards.q: Why different glucocorticoids produce the same effects
cards.a: GR is widely distributed; no tissue specificity between agents

cards.q: Example of a rapid, non-genomic glucocorticoid action
cards.a: Inhibition of ACTH release from the pituitary

cards.q: Route for corticoids, with the exception
cards.a: All oral except DOCA; water-soluble esters can be given i.v.

cards.q: Hydrocortisone protein binding and main carrier
cards.a: About 90%, mainly cortisol-binding globulin (transcortin) and albumin

cards.q: Conditions that raise total but not free cortisol
cards.a: Pregnancy and oral contraceptives (raise transcortin)

cards.q: Site where corticoids are metabolised
cards.a: Liver (microsomal enzymes)

cards.q: Plasma half-life of hydrocortisone
cards.a: About 1.5 hours; biological action lasts longer

cards.q: Why synthetic corticoids last longer
cards.a: Resistant to hepatic metabolism

cards.q: Drugs that speed corticoid metabolism
cards.a: Phenobarbitone and phenytoin (enzyme inducers)

cards.q: Effect of fluorination at position 9 or 6
cards.a: Gives highly potent corticoids

cards.q: Relative potency of prednisolone to hydrocortisone
cards.a: Prednisolone about 4 times more potent

cards.q: Key feature of hydrocortisone
cards.a: Short acting; significant mineralocorticoid activity too

cards.q: Methylprednisolone compared with prednisolone
cards.a: Slightly more potent and more selective

cards.q: Dexamethasone profile
cards.a: Very potent, highly selective, long acting; little fluid retention

cards.q: Deflazacort profile
cards.a: Less glucocorticoid potency than prednisolone; no mineralocorticoid activity

cards.q: Only pure mineralocorticoid among the systemic corticoids listed
cards.a: DOCA (desoxycorticosterone acetate)

cards.q: Fludrocortisone profile
cards.a: Potent mineralocorticoid with some glucocorticoid action; oral

cards.q: Why aldosterone is not used clinically
cards.a: Poor oral bioavailability and difficult dose control

cards.q: Anti-inflammatory dose equal to hydrocortisone 20 mg: prednisolone
cards.a: 5 mg

cards.q: Anti-inflammatory dose equal to hydrocortisone 20 mg: methylprednisolone
cards.a: 4 mg

cards.q: Anti-inflammatory dose equal to hydrocortisone 20 mg: triamcinolone
cards.a: 4 mg

cards.q: Anti-inflammatory dose equal to hydrocortisone 20 mg: deflazacort
cards.a: 6 mg

cards.q: Anti-inflammatory dose equal to hydrocortisone 20 mg: dexamethasone
Anti-inflammatory dose equal to hydrocortisone 20 mg: betamethasone
Systemic glucocorticoids: list all named in the chapter
cards.a: Hydrocortisone, prednisolone, methylprednisolone, triamcinolone, deflazacort, dexamethasone, betamethasone

cards.q: Mineralocorticoids: list all named in the chapter
cards.a: DOCA, fludrocortisone, aldosterone

cards.q: Inhaled or topical glucocorticoids named: list
cards.a: Beclomethasone dipropionate, budesonide, fluticasone (plus fluocinolone, clobetasol)

cards.q: Long-acting glucocorticoids (biological half-life over 36 hours)
cards.a: Dexamethasone and betamethasone

cards.q: Short-acting glucocorticoid (biological half-life under 12 hours)
cards.a: Hydrocortisone

cards.q: Intermediate-acting glucocorticoid with less HPA suppression on a single morning dose
cards.a: Prednisolone

cards.q: Glucocorticoid used as 1 g i.v. pulse every 6-8 weeks
cards.a: Methylprednisolone

cards.q: Glucocorticoid that does not add to urinary steroid metabolites at suppressive doses
cards.a: Dexamethasone

cards.q: Drug of choice for chronic adrenal insufficiency (Addison's disease)
cards.a: Oral hydrocortisone, with salt and water

cards.q: Add-on mineralocorticoid in Addison's when Na+ loss persists
cards.a: Fludrocortisone

cards.q: Acute adrenal insufficiency first-line drug and dose
cards.a: Hydrocortisone 100 mg i.v. bolus, then infusion (or dexamethasone 8-16 mg)

cards.q: Enzyme most often deficient in congenital adrenal hyperplasia
cards.a: 21-hydroxylase

cards.q: Congenital adrenal hyperplasia treatment
cards.a: Hydrocortisone 0.6 mg/kg daily in divided doses; fludrocortisone if salt wasting

cards.q: Corticoid of choice where fluid retention must be avoided
cards.a: Dexamethasone or betamethasone

cards.q: Role of corticoids in rheumatoid arthritis
cards.a: Only severe cases, as adjuvant to NSAIDs

cards.q: Corticoid use in chronic gout
cards.a: Not recommended, despite uricosuric action

cards.q: Corticoid role in anaphylaxis
cards.a: Adjunct only; adrenaline acts immediately, corticoids take 1-2 hours

cards.q: Dose and drug for autoimmune haemolytic anaemia, ITP and chronic hepatitis
cards.a: Prednisolone 1-2 mg/kg/day until remission, then taper

cards.q: Corticoid used with neostigmine in myasthenia gravis
cards.a: Adjunct to neostigmine in severe cases

cards.q: Systemic corticoid use in status asthmaticus
cards.a: i.v. glucocorticoid, withdrawn when emergency is over

cards.q: Corticoid given to mother to mature fetal lungs
cards.a: Betamethasone 12 mg i.m., two doses 18-24 hours apart, when delivery is expected before 34 weeks

cards.q: Why betamethasone or dexamethasone are preferred for fetal lung maturity
cards.a: Higher placental transfer than prednisolone

cards.q: Infections where corticoids are used under chemotherapy cover
cards.a: Severe TB (miliary, meningeal), severe lepra reaction, bacterial meningitis, PCP with hypoxia in AIDS

cards.q: Eye condition where steroids are contraindicated
cards.a: Herpes simplex keratitis and ocular injuries

cards.q: Eye conditions needing systemic steroid
cards.a: Retinitis, optic neuritis, uveitis

cards.q: Skin conditions needing systemic corticoid
cards.a: Pemphigus vulgaris, exfoliative dermatitis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome

cards.q: Corticoid role in inflammatory bowel disease
cards.a: Acute phases, with sulfasalazine or mesalazine; retention enema for colon

cards.q: Corticoid choice for cerebral oedema
cards.a: Dexamethasone or betamethasone (no Na+ retention)

cards.q: Corticoid use in Bell's palsy and MS relapse
cards.a: Oral prednisolone 2-4 weeks; methylprednisolone 1 g i.v. daily for 2-3 days in MS

cards.q: Corticoid added in neurocysticercosis treatment
cards.a: Prednisolone 40 mg/day for 2-4 weeks with albendazole or praziquantel

cards.q: Corticoid added to antiemetic in highly emetogenic chemotherapy
cards.a: Dexamethasone 8-20 mg i.v. with ondansetron or metoclopramide

cards.q: Haematological malignancies where corticoids are essential
cards.a: Acute lymphatic leukaemia, Hodgkin's and other lymphomas

cards.q: Drugs preferred over corticoids for malignancy hypercalcaemia
cards.a: Bisphosphonates (more effective)

cards.q: Corticoid use in septic shock now
cards.a: High dose abandoned; low-dose hydrocortisone for relative adrenal insufficiency

cards.q: Corticoid role in thyroid storm
cards.a: Hydrocortisone 100 mg i.v. 8-hourly; reduces T4 to T3 conversion

cards.q: Corticoid-induced osteoporosis: most effective drugs
cards.a: Bisphosphonates

cards.q: Mineralocorticoid excess effects that are now rare
cards.a: Sodium and water retention, oedema, hypokalaemic alkalosis, rising BP

cards.q: Cushing's habitus features
cards.a: Rounded face, supraclavicular hump, truncal obesity, thin limbs

cards.q: Skin changes from prolonged corticoid use
cards.a: Fragile skin, purple striae (thighs, lower abdomen), bruising, telangiectasia, hirsutism

cards.q: Diet advised with corticoid therapy longer than 2 weeks
cards.a: High protein, high potassium

cards.q: Infection risk with corticoids
cards.a: Non-specific; latent TB can flare; opportunistic Candida

cards.q: Peptic ulcer risk with corticoids
cards.a: About doubled; silent perforation possible

cards.q: Bone adverse effect of corticoids
cards.a: Osteoporosis: vertebral compression and long-bone fractures, especially in the elderly

cards.q: Joint complication of high-dose corticoids
cards.a: Avascular necrosis of femoral head, humerus or knee

cards.q: Eye adverse effects of corticoids
cards.a: Posterior subcapsular cataract (after years) and glaucoma (prolonged topical use)

cards.q: Growth effect of corticoids in children
cards.a: Retardation even at small doses over long periods; GH suppression also

cards.q: Corticoid of choice in pregnancy for fetal exposure
cards.a: Prednisolone (inactivated by placenta, less fetal exposure)

cards.q: Pregnancy complications linked to prolonged corticoids
cards.a: Gestational diabetes, pregnancy-induced hypertension, pre-eclampsia

cards.q: Psychiatric risks of long-term corticoids
cards.a: Mood change, sleep loss, rarely manic psychosis or depression

cards.q: Withdrawal syndrome after stopping corticoids
cards.a: Malaise, fever, anorexia, postural hypotension, myalgia, reactivation of disease

cards.q: Dose and duration that call for gradual withdrawal
cards.a: Hydrocortisone over 20-25 mg/day or prednisolone 5 mg/day for over 2-3 weeks

cards.q: Withdrawal taper step for hydrocortisone
cards.a: Reduce by 20 mg/day each week, then smaller steps

cards.q: Duration of stress-cover risk after corticoid withdrawal
cards.a: Up to one year

cards.q: Action when infection occurs on corticoids
cards.a: Do not stop; dose may need to be increased

cards.q: Surgery in a patient on long-term corticoids
cards.a: Cover with i.v. hydrocortisone peri-operatively, then oral prednisolone

cards.q: Measure to reduce HPA axis suppression: drug and dose
cards.a: Shorter-acting agent (hydrocortisone, prednisolone) at lowest possible dose

cards.q: Measure to reduce HPA axis suppression: duration and timing
cards.a: Shortest possible period; give whole daily dose in the morning

cards.q: Alternate-day regimen advantage
cards.a: Less HPA suppression and less immunosuppression (lower infection risk)

cards.q: Agents not suited to alternate-day therapy
cards.a: Long-acting agents such as dexamethasone

cards.q: Local steroids with poor systemic availability (listed)
cards.a: Beclomethasone dipropionate, triamcinolone acetonide, fluticasone

cards.q: Relative contraindications to corticoids: list all
cards.a: Peptic ulcer, diabetes, hypertension, viral and fungal infections, TB and other infections, osteoporosis, herpes simplex keratitis, psychosis, epilepsy, CHF, renal failure

cards.q: Metyrapone mechanism and test use
cards.a: Blocks 11-beta-hydroxylase; raises ACTH; tests pituitary responsiveness

cards.q: Steroidogenesis inhibitors used in Cushing's: list
cards.a: Aminoglutethimide, trilostane, high-dose ketoconazole

cards.q: Glucocorticoid receptor blocker used in Cushing's
cards.a: Mifepristone (for inoperable adrenal carcinoma or ectopic ACTH)

cards.q: Why GR blockade by mifepristone is partly overcome
cards.a: Feedback loss raises ACTH, so more cortisol is made

cards.q: Testicular cells that secrete testosterone
cards.a: Leydig (interstitial) cells, under LH

cards.q: Testosterone output of the adult male testes per day
cards.a: About 5-12 mg

cards.q: Enzyme converting testosterone to dihydrotestosterone
cards.a: 5-alpha reductase

cards.q: Adrenal weak androgens and their relative potency
cards.a: DHEA and androstenedione; about 1/20 to 1/30 of testosterone; act via conversion

cards.q: Ovarian plus adrenal-derived testosterone in women per day
Androsterone potency relative to testosterone
cards.a: About 1/10; a urinary metabolite

cards.q: Hormone that drives spermatogenesis in Sertoli cells
cards.a: FSH

cards.q: Effect of high testosterone levels on pituitary and Leydig cells
cards.a: Inhibits LH secretion; long-term Leydig cell atrophy

cards.q: Androgen that is active itself in the foetal genital rudiments
cards.a: Testosterone

cards.q: Sites where testosterone itself is the active hormone (list)
cards.a: Foetal genital rudiments, hypothalamus-pituitary feedback, erythroid cells, spermatogenic cells

cards.q: Why dihydrotestosterone binds the androgen receptor better
cards.a: Binds more avidly than testosterone; the complex is more active

cards.q: Enzyme isoform predominant in genital skin and male urogenital tract
cards.a: 5-alpha reductase type 2 (finasteride-sensitive)

cards.q: Genetic loss of 5-alpha reductase type 2 causes
cards.a: Male pseudohermaphroditism

cards.q: Testosterone conversion to estradiol that drives epiphyseal fusion
cards.a: Aromatisation (estradiol, not testosterone, fuses epiphyses)

cards.q: Hormone that increases erythropoietin and haem synthesis
cards.a: Testosterone (higher haematocrit in men)

cards.q: Why oral testosterone is inactive
cards.a: High first-pass metabolism in liver

cards.q: Plasma half-life of testosterone
cards.a: 10-20 minutes

cards.q: Testosterone ester that is short acting
cards.a: Testosterone propionate (daily to twice weekly)

cards.q: Testosterone esters that are long acting (listed)
cards.a: Enanthate, cypionate, isocaproate, decanoate (every 2-4 weeks)

cards.q: Oral androgen absorbed through lymphatics, bypassing liver
cards.a: Testosterone undecanoate

cards.q: Oral 17-alkyl androgens with cholestatic jaundice risk (listed)
cards.a: Methyltestosterone and fluoxymesterone

cards.q: Transdermal dihydrotestosterone gel product and dose
cards.a: Andractim 25 mg/g gel, once daily on non-scrotal skin

cards.q: Androgen adverse effect in women
cards.a: Virilisation, excess body hair, menstrual irregularity; voice change may be permanent

cards.q: Androgen effect that wears off early in therapy
cards.a: Frequent, painful erections (subside spontaneously)

cards.q: Sperm effect of moderate androgen doses
cards.a: Oligozoospermia in men with normal testosterone, given for a few weeks

cards.q: Androgen contraindications: cancers
cards.a: Carcinoma of prostate and male breast

cards.q: Androgen contraindications: organ and pregnancy
cards.a: Liver and kidney disease, pregnancy (masculinises female foetus)

cards.q: Androgen caution: age and cardiac disease
cards.a: Avoid in men over 65 and in coronary artery disease or CHF

cards.q: Androgens can worsen these three conditions
cards.a: Sleep apnoea, migraine, epilepsy

cards.q: Androgen use in primary testicular failure
cards.a: Courses of 4-6 months; high dose accelerates epiphyseal closure

cards.q: Androgen use in hereditary angioneurotic oedema
cards.a: Prevents attacks by raising C1 esterase inhibitor (17-alkyl agents, not testosterone)

cards.q: Androgen use in AIDS wasting
cards.a: Improves weakness and wasting in patients with low testosterone

cards.q: Evidence for oral androgens in male infertility
cards.a: Meta-analysis of 11 trials: no effect on sperm count, motility or pregnancy rate

cards.q: Mesterolone property and use
cards.a: Less feedback inhibition of gonadotropins; promoted for male infertility

cards.q: Testosterone undecanoate product use
cards.a: Male hypogonadism and osteoporosis, 40 mg capsules

cards.q: Anabolic to androgenic ratio reference point and method
cards.a: Testosterone = 1; measured in castrated rats by levator ani versus ventral prostate weight

cards.q: Anabolic selectivity of anabolic steroids in rats
cards.a: Modest, about 1 to 3; lower in man

cards.q: Adverse effects specific to 17-alkyl anabolic steroids
cards.a: Jaundice and worsened lipid profile

cards.q: Anabolic steroid use in catabolic states
cards.a: Reduces N loss short term; long-term benefit doubtful

cards.q: Drug preferred over anabolic steroids for osteoporosis
cards.a: Bisphosphonates

cards.q: Growth-promoting drug preferred over anabolic steroids in short boys
cards.a: Somatotropin

cards.q: Anabolic steroids: list all named
cards.a: Nandrolone, oxymetholone, stanozolol, methandienone

cards.q: Androgens (testosterone-based) named in the chapter: list
cards.a: Testosterone, testosterone propionate, enanthate, cypionate, decanoate, undecanoate, methyltestosterone, fluoxymesterone, mesterolone

cards.q: Antiandrogen that acts by competitive AR block and raises LH
cards.a: Flutamide (its metabolite 2-hydroxyflutamide)

cards.q: Flutamide dose
cards.a: 250 mg three times daily

cards.q: Nonsteroidal antiandrogen with longer half-life, once daily dosing
cards.a: Bicalutamide (half-life about 6 days; 50 mg daily)

cards.q: Long-acting antiandrogen similar to bicalutamide and flutamide
cards.a: Nilutamide

cards.q: Steroidal antiandrogen related to progesterone that lowers LH by progestational action
cards.a: Cyproterone acetate

cards.q: Cyproterone acetate uses
cards.a: Precocious puberty in boys, inappropriate sexual behaviour, acne and hirsutism in women (with an estrogen)

cards.q: Cyproterone plus ethinylestradiol 35 mcg use
cards.a: Cyclic contraceptive for women

cards.q: Antiandrogen effect of GnRH superagonists
cards.a: Lose androgen secretion after a few days of administration

cards.q: Antiandrogen toxicity limiting use at high dose
cards.a: Ketoconazole (high dose inhibits steroidogenesis; toxic)

cards.q: Drugs with weak antiandrogen effect causing side effects (listed)
cards.a: Cimetidine, spironolactone, progesterone

cards.q: Antiandrogens named in the chapter: list
cards.a: Cyproterone acetate, flutamide, bicalutamide, nilutamide (plus ketoconazole, cimetidine, spironolactone as weak)

cards.q: Second-generation nonsteroidal androgen receptor antagonists for prostate cancer: list
cards.a: Enzalutamide, apalutamide, darolutamide

cards.q: 5-alpha reductase inhibitor (competitive) and its selectivity
cards.a: Finasteride; selective for type 2 isoenzyme

cards.q: Effect of finasteride on plasma testosterone and LH
cards.a: DHT falls; plasma LH and testosterone unchanged

cards.q: Finasteride use in benign prostatic hyperplasia
cards.a: Reduces prostate size; relief in about 50%; takes about 6 months; works on static component

cards.q: Prostate volume above which finasteride gives more relief
cards.a: Over 40 mL

cards.q: Finasteride dose in BPH and in alopecia
cards.a: 5 mg daily (BPH); 1 mg daily (male pattern baldness)

cards.q: Finasteride adverse effects (common, rare)
cards.a: Decreased libido, impotence, reduced ejaculate volume (3-4%); gynaecomastia rare

cards.q: Dutasteride enzyme inhibition
cards.a: Inhibits both type 1 and type 2 5-alpha reductase and lowers DHT

cards.q: Dutasteride elimination half-life
cards.a: About 9 weeks; metabolised by CYP3A4

cards.q: Dutasteride dose
cards.a: 0.5 mg daily

cards.q: Prostate cancer risk reduction with 5-alpha reductase inhibitors
cards.a: Up to 25% (finasteride and dutasteride)

cards.q: Why alpha-1 blockers and finasteride are used together in BPH
cards.a: Finasteride acts on static, alpha-1 blockers on dynamic obstruction

cards.q: Fixed-dose testosterone with yohimbine, strychnine and vitamins status in India
cards.a: Banned

cards.q: Testosterone ester preparation with three esters and depot interval (listed)
cards.a: Sustanon 250 (testosterone propionate, phenylpropionate, isocaproate, decanoate), every 3-4 weeks

cards.q: Main mediator of penile smooth muscle relaxation
cards.a: Nitric oxide (from NANC nerves and endothelium)

cards.q: Other mediators of erection besides NO
cards.a: Acetylcholine and prostaglandins

cards.q: Second messenger raised by NO and degraded by PDE-5
cards.a: cGMP

cards.q: First-line drug class for erectile dysfunction
cards.a: PDE-5 inhibitors

cards.q: PDE-5 inhibitors named in the chapter: list
cards.a: Sildenafil, tadalafil, vardenafil

cards.q: Sildenafil approval timeline
cards.a: Marketed in USA in 1998, India two years later

cards.q: Sildenafil bioavailability and peak
cards.a: About 40%; peak in 1-2 hours

cards.q: Sildenafil half-life in men under 65
cards.a: About 4 hours

cards.q: Sildenafil starting dose and dose in men over 65
cards.a: 50 mg (25 mg over 65); may increase to 100 mg 1 hour before intercourse

cards.q: Sildenafil effect without sexual stimulation
cards.a: No effect on erection in absence of sexual activity

cards.q: Sildenafil off-target enzyme and visual effect
cards.a: PDE-6 inhibition: impaired blue-green colour discrimination

cards.q: Major fatal interaction with sildenafil
cards.a: Nitrates: precipitous BP fall and MI

cards.q: Sildenafil safety signal in US reporting by 2002
cards.a: 130 deaths reported; most with risk factors or interactions

cards.q: Drugs that potentiate sildenafil (listed)
cards.a: Erythromycin, ketoconazole, verapamil, cimetidine

cards.q: Conditions predisposing to priapism with sildenafil
cards.a: Leukaemia, sickle cell anaemia, myeloma

cards.q: Tadalafil profile
cards.a: Longer acting: half-life about 18 hours; duration 24-36 hours; dose 10 mg (max 20 mg)

cards.q: Gap before nitrates after a PDE-5 inhibitor
cards.a: 24 hours after sildenafil; up to 3 days after tadalafil (GG14: over 24 hours, especially tadalafil)

cards.q: Vardenafil dose and QT effect
cards.a: 10 mg (elderly 5 mg, max 20 mg); prolongs QT interval

cards.q: Drugs to avoid with vardenafil (listed)
cards.a: Class IA and class III antiarrhythmics; hyperkalaemia; long QT

cards.q: Sildenafil dose in pulmonary arterial hypertension
cards.a: 20 mg three times daily (drug of choice for PAH)

cards.q: Endothelin receptor antagonist for PAH named in chapter
cards.a: Ambrisentan

cards.q: Papaverine and phentolamine injection (PIPE): main risk
cards.a: Priapism in 2-15%; reversed by aspiration or local phenylephrine

cards.q: Prostaglandin used intracavernosally for ED
cards.a: Alprostadil (PGE1); erection lasts 1-2 hours

cards.q: ED group where alprostadil is most used
cards.a: Patients not responding to PDE-5 inhibitors (neurogenic, psychogenic)

cards.q: Transurethral form of alprostaglandin for ED and its drawback
cards.a: MUSE pellet; less effective, may cause urethral burning

cards.q: Role of androgens in ED
cards.a: Only if androgen deficiency is proven

cards.q: Major ovarian estrogen and its site of synthesis
cards.a: Estradiol; made in graafian follicle, corpus luteum and placenta

cards.q: Order of estrogen metabolism in liver
cards.a: Estradiol to estrone to estriol (all three active; estradiol most potent)

cards.q: Estrogen daily output in menstruating women
cards.a: 10-100 micrograms, varies with cycle phase

cards.q: Placental estrogen peak at term and main types
cards.a: Up to 30 mg/day; mainly estrone and estriol

cards.q: Source of postmenopausal estrogen
cards.a: Extraglandular aromatisation of adrenal androgens (2-10 micrograms/day)

cards.q: Estrogen effect on uterus and cervix
cards.a: Endometrial proliferation; watery alkaline cervical mucus favouring sperm

cards.q: Effect of continuous low-dose estrogen without progestin
cards.a: Endometrial hypertrophy; delayed menses with irregular breakthrough bleeding

cards.q: Normal trigger of menstruation
cards.a: Progesterone withdrawal

cards.q: Estrogen effect on myometrium sensitivity
cards.a: Sensitises uterus to oxytocin

cards.q: Estrogen effect on lipids
cards.a: Lowers LDL; raises HDL and triglycerides

cards.q: Clotting factors induced by estrogen
cards.a: Factors II, VII, IX and X (raised coagulability)

cards.q: Vascular mediators induced by estrogen
cards.a: Nitric oxide synthase and PGI2 in endothelium

cards.q: Estrogen receptor subtypes and their main sites
cards.a: ER-alpha in uterus, vagina, breast, bone; ER-beta in prostate and ovaries

cards.q: Estrogen plasma carrier raised without true hormonal change
cards.a: SHBG, TBG, CBG

cards.q: Estrogen dose equivalence: estradiol 0.1 mg equals
cards.a: Ethinylestradiol 0.1 mg; mestranol 0.15 mg; conjugated estrogens 10 mg

cards.q: Oral potency of estradiol
cards.a: Inactive orally (first-pass metabolism)

cards.q: Ethinylestradiol pharmacokinetics
cards.a: Orally active and more potent; slow metabolism, half-life 12-24 hours

cards.q: Usual dose of conjugated estrogens in HRT (listed)
cards.a: 0.625 mg/day (Premarin)

cards.q: Transdermal estradiol patch dose for menopause
cards.a: 0.05 mg/day (24-hour patch, changed every 3-4 days)

cards.q: Estradiol patch sizes and delivery per 24 hours
Advantage of transdermal over oral estradiol
cards.a: Avoids high hepatic delivery; TBG, CBG and angiotensinogen not raised

cards.q: Fosfestrol use
cards.a: Carcinoma of prostate (palliative), given i.v. or orally

cards.q: Estrogen used for vaginal atrophy and its agent
cards.a: Dienestrol 0.01% vaginal cream

cards.q: Estrogen adverse effects in males
cards.a: Loss of libido, gynaecomastia, feminisation

cards.q: Estrogen effect on children
cards.a: Epiphyseal fusion and reduced adult stature

cards.q: Endometrial carcinoma risk with unopposed estrogen in postmenopausal women
cards.a: About 5-15 fold

cards.q: Estrogen contraindication
cards.a: Pregnancy

cards.q: Menopausal symptoms treated by HRT (listed first)
cards.a: Vasomotor symptoms (hot flashes, sweating); urogenital atrophy; osteoporosis

cards.q: Main indication of HRT in current guidance
cards.a: Vasomotor and other menopausal symptoms, before 60 years or within 10 years of menopause

cards.q: HRT dosing principle
cards.a: Smallest effective dose for the shortest duration

cards.q: Who needs estrogen alone in HRT
cards.a: Hysterectomised women

cards.q: Who needs estrogen plus progestin in HRT
cards.a: Women with an intact uterus

cards.q: Type of HRT for perimenopausal women
cards.a: Cyclic, not continuous

cards.q: HRT protection against coronary disease
cards.a: Only in early postmenopausal women

cards.q: Effect of HRT on osteoporosis prevention
cards.a: Not the best option; bisphosphonates preferred; avoid beyond 5 years or over 60

cards.q: Cognitive effect of HRT in older women (WHIMS)
cards.a: No protection; dementia incidence roughly doubled

cards.q: Venous thromboembolism risk on HRT in older women (HERS)
cards.a: Roughly tripled

cards.q: Cancers linked to combined HRT
cards.a: Breast cancer (and endometrial if unopposed)

cards.q: Non-cancer risks of HRT named in chapter
cards.a: Gallstones (estrogen); migraine (progestins)

cards.q: Tibolone: class and purpose
cards.a: 19-norsteroid designed for HRT; estrogenic, progestational and weak androgenic metabolites

cards.q: Tibolone dose
cards.a: 2.5 mg daily (Livial)

cards.q: Steroid name for the natural progestin
cards.a: Progesterone (21 carbon, from cholesterol)

cards.q: Source and daily output of progesterone in cycle
cards.a: Corpus luteum, 10-20 mg/day, second half of cycle, under LH

cards.q: Progesterone plasma half-life
cards.a: 5-7 minutes; main metabolite pregnanediol

cards.q: Progesterone effect on endometrium
cards.a: Secretory changes in estrogen-primed endometrium; halts epithelial proliferation

cards.q: Progesterone effect on cervical mucus
cards.a: Makes it viscid, scanty and hostile to sperm

cards.q: Progesterone effect on body temperature
cards.a: Raises about 0.5 degrees C (luteal phase)

cards.q: Progesterone effect on GnRH pulses
cards.a: Reduces pulse frequency; prevents preovulatory LH surge if given in follicular phase

cards.q: Progesterone receptor distribution
cards.a: Limited: female genital tract, breast, CNS, pituitary

cards.q: Progesterone route and reason
cards.a: Oily i.m. injection; oral only as micronized form (absorbed via lymphatics)

cards.q: Progesterone effect on lipids
cards.a: Does not lower HDL; micronized form leaves estrogen HDL/LDL benefit intact

cards.q: Synthetic progestins that are prodrugs
cards.a: Desogestrel and norgestimate

cards.q: Synthetic progestin with weak antiandrogenic, weaker antiovulatory, strong endometrial antiestrogenic action
cards.a: Nomegestrol acetate

cards.q: Estrane (19-nortestosterone) progestins listed
cards.a: Norethindrone (norethisterone), lynestrenol, allylestrenol

cards.q: Gonane progestins listed
cards.a: Levonorgestrel, desogestrel, norgestimate, gestodene

cards.q: Synthetic progestins: list all named in the chapter
cards.a: Norethindrone, lynestrenol, allylestrenol, levonorgestrel, desogestrel, norgestimate, gestodene, nomegestrol, medroxyprogesterone acetate, megestrol acetate, dydrogesterone, hydroxyprogesterone caproate

cards.q: Progesterone derivatives used as adjuvant to estrogens in HRT (listed)
cards.a: Medroxyprogesterone acetate, megestrol acetate, dydrogesterone, hydroxyprogesterone caproate

cards.q: Progestin added to HRT in non-hysterectomised women and duration
cards.a: Micronized oral progesterone (or similar) for 10-12 days each month

cards.q: Progestin for dysfunctional uterine bleeding
cards.a: Large doses to stop bleeding, then cyclic lower doses; progestin with estrogenic action preferred

cards.q: Continuous progestin use in endometriosis
cards.a: Induces anovulatory, hypoestrogenic state by suppressing gonadotropins

cards.q: Drug for premenstrual dysphoric disorder on symptom days
cards.a: Fluoxetine and other SSRIs

cards.q: Progestin use in threatened or habitual abortion
cards.a: Most patients have no progesterone deficiency; only if deficiency proven

cards.q: Progestins in advanced endometrial carcinoma
cards.a: Palliative in about 50% of cases; high doses needed

cards.q: Progestin adverse effects at higher doses (listed)
cards.a: Breast engorgement, headache, temperature rise, oedema, reflux, acne, mood swings

cards.q: Progestin effect on HDL with 19-nortestosterone derivatives
cards.a: Lowers HDL and raises LDL; progesterone itself does not

cards.q: Progestin use contraindicated for
cards.a: Diagnosis of pregnancy

cards.q: Progestin effect in early pregnancy on fetus
cards.a: Masculinisation of female foetus and congenital abnormalities

cards.q: Danazol: class and main action
cards.a: Isoxazole derivative of ethisterone; suppresses gonadotropins, so inhibits ovarian and testicular function

cards.q: Danazol use in endometriosis
cards.a: Improves about 75%; relief of dysmenorrhoea prompt; first line is estrogen-progestin pill

cards.q: Danazol use in menorrhagia
cards.a: Reduces blood loss; second line after oral progestin

cards.q: Danazol use in fibrocystic breast disease
cards.a: Improves about 75% in 3-6 months

cards.q: Danazol adverse effects (androgenic)
cards.a: Acne, hirsutism, voice deepening, weight gain, loss of breast size, hot flashes, cramps

cards.q: Clomiphene isomer that is a pure estrogen antagonist
cards.a: Trans isomer (enclomiphene); cis isomer (zuclomiphene) weakly agonistic in rats

cards.q: Mechanism by which clomiphene induces gonadotropin release
cards.a: Blocks estrogen negative feedback at the pituitary

cards.q: Clomiphene use for ovulation failure
cards.a: 50 mg daily for 5 days from day 5 of cycle, monthly; max 6 cycles

cards.q: Ovulation induction in PCOS: drug with higher pregnancy and live-birth rate than clomiphene (GG14)
cards.a: Letrozole (KDT: India banned it for ovulation induction in 2011)

cards.q: Clomiphene add-on that improves success in anovulatory women
cards.a: hMG or hCG on the last 2 days of the course

cards.q: Clomiphene plasma half-life and excretion
cards.a: About 6 days; stored in fat, excreted in bile

cards.q: Clomiphene adverse effects
cards.a: Polycystic ovaries, multiple pregnancy, hot flashes, vertigo; possible ovarian tumour risk

cards.q: Clomiphene male use
cards.a: Male infertility: 25 mg daily for 24 days a month, up to 6 months

cards.q: Fulvestrant class and use
cards.a: Selective estrogen receptor downregulator (SERD); ER+ breast cancer after tamoxifen failure

cards.q: Fulvestrant dose and half-life
cards.a: 250-500 mg monthly i.m.; half-life over a month

cards.q: Tamoxifen actions by tissue
cards.a: Antagonist in breast and blood vessels; partial agonist in uterus, bone, liver, pituitary

cards.q: Tamoxifen dose
cards.a: 20 mg/day (max 40 mg/day)

cards.q: Tamoxifen half-life pattern
cards.a: Biphasic: about 10 hours and 7 days; excreted mainly in bile

cards.q: Tamoxifen use in primary breast cancer prophylaxis
cards.a: High-risk women; about 45% reduction in ER+ breast cancer

cards.q: Tamoxifen adverse effect with clotting
cards.a: Increases venous thromboembolism 2-3 times (estrogenic action on clotting)

cards.q: Tamoxifen adverse effects (common)
cards.a: Hot flashes, vomiting, rash, vaginal bleeding, menstrual irregularity

cards.q: Tamoxifen effect on serum lipids
cards.a: Lowers total and LDL cholesterol; HDL and triglycerides unchanged

cards.q: Tamoxifen effect on bone
cards.a: Anti-resorptive, improves bone mass

cards.q: Tamoxifen male use
cards.a: Alternative to clomiphene for male infertility

cards.q: Tamoxifen newer congener with weaker agonism
cards.a: Toremifene

cards.q: Raloxifene tissue profile
cards.a: Partial estrogen agonist in bone, lipids, CVS; antagonist in endometrium and breast

cards.q: Raloxifene dose
cards.a: 60 mg/day

cards.q: Raloxifene effect on vertebral fracture
cards.a: Halves vertebral fracture risk; no protection for long bones

cards.q: Raloxifene effect on breast cancer
cards.a: Reduces risk by about 65%, in ER+ tumours only

cards.q: Raloxifene effect on lipids
cards.a: Lowers LDL; no rise in HDL or triglycerides

cards.q: Raloxifene effect on endometrium
cards.a: No proliferation; no increase in endometrial carcinoma

cards.q: Raloxifene effect on menopausal hot flashes
cards.a: No relief; may induce hot flashes

cards.q: Raloxifene half-life and excretion
cards.a: About 28 hours; excreted in faeces; low bioavailability (first-pass glucuronidation)

cards.q: Raloxifene serious adverse effect
cards.a: About 3-fold increase in deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism

cards.q: Raloxifene place in osteoporosis
cards.a: Second-line drug in postmenopausal women

cards.q: Aromatase: final step of estrogen synthesis converts
cards.a: Androgens (testosterone and androstenedione) to estrogens (A-ring aromatisation)

cards.q: Letrozole type and mechanism
cards.a: Nonsteroidal, reversible (type 2) aromatase inhibitor; near-total estrogen deprivation in postmenopausal women

cards.q: Letrozole dose
cards.a: 2.5 mg daily

cards.q: Anastrozole type and dose
cards.a: Nonsteroidal, reversible (type 2); 1 mg once daily; more potent than letrozole

cards.q: Anastrozole peak effect
cards.a: Accumulates; peak effect after 7-10 days

cards.q: Exemestane type and mechanism
cards.a: Steroidal, irreversible (type 1) suicide inhibitor; over 90% estradiol suppression

cards.q: Exemestane dose
cards.a: 25 mg daily after meals; 50 mg with CYP3A4 inducers

cards.q: Exemestane androgenic property
cards.a: Weak androgenic activity, like androstenedione

cards.q: AI use in premenopausal women
cards.a: Not recommended unless ovaries removed or gonadotropins suppressed

cards.q: AI adverse effects on bone and joints
cards.a: Accelerated bone loss, fractures, arthritic symptoms

cards.q: AI effect on endometrium and VTE
cards.a: No endometrial hyperplasia; no increase in venous thromboembolism

cards.q: AI versus tamoxifen in tamoxifen failure
cards.a: AIs effective in tamoxifen failure; tamoxifen not

cards.q: Tamoxifen versus AI for lipid profile
cards.a: Tamoxifen improves lipids; AIs have no effect

cards.q: Aromatase inhibitors named in the chapter: list
cards.a: Letrozole, anastrozole, exemestane

cards.q: SERMs named in the chapter: list
cards.a: Tamoxifen, toremifene, raloxifene (ormeloxifene in contraception)

cards.q: SERD named in the chapter
cards.a: Fulvestrant

cards.q: Antiestrogens named in the chapter, with type
cards.a: Clomiphene (partial), fulvestrant (pure antagonist)

cards.q: Mifepristone class and receptor action
cards.a: 19-norsteroid; competitive antagonist and partial agonist at PR (A and B); antiglucocorticoid, antiandrogenic

cards.q: Mifepristone effect in follicular phase
cards.a: Blunts mid-cycle gonadotropin surge; delays or prevents ovulation

cards.q: Mifepristone bioavailability and metabolism
cards.a: About 25%; CYP3A4; half-life 20-36 hours

cards.q: Mifepristone regimen for termination of pregnancy up to 7 weeks
cards.a: 600 mg oral, then misoprostol 400 micrograms 48 hours later (over 90% success)

cards.q: Mifepristone use to ripen cervix
cards.a: 600 mg 24-30 hours before surgical abortion or labour induction

cards.q: Mifepristone postcoital use
cards.a: 600 mg within 72 hours; highly effective emergency contraceptive

cards.q: Mifepristone once-monthly contraceptive dose
cards.a: 200 mg two days after midcycle (luteolysis); not for regular use

cards.q: Mifepristone use for labour induction
cards.a: Blocks progesterone relaxant effect; for intrauterine fetal death

cards.q: Mifepristone role in Cushing's
cards.a: Palliative only; low efficacy; for non-resectable tumour

cards.q: Mifepristone-misoprostol kit for medical abortion (up to 49 days): how it is taken
cards.a: Day 1: mifepristone three 200 mg tablets (600 mg); day 3: misoprostol two 200 microgram tablets (400 micrograms)

cards.q: Ulipristal class and use
cards.a: Selective progesterone receptor modulator (SPRM); emergency contraceptive 30 mg

cards.q: Ulipristal side effects
cards.a: Headache, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, menstrual delay; rare ovarian cysts

cards.q: Ulipristal antiglucocorticoid strength versus mifepristone
cards.a: Weaker

cards.q: Pure progesterone antagonist listed
cards.a: Onapristone

cards.q: Antiprogestin more effective in endometriosis
cards.a: Gestrinone

cards.q: Antiprogestins and SPRMs named in the chapter: list
cards.a: Mifepristone, ulipristal, onapristone, gestrinone

cards.q: Hormonal contraceptive effect that the estrogen adds to a progestin pill
cards.a: Enhances efficacy; combined pills became most popular

cards.q: Combined pill regimen and most popular form
cards.a: Fixed-dose estrogen and progestin for all days; calendar packs (monophasic)

cards.q: Ethinylestradiol dose threshold in combined pills
cards.a: 30 micrograms daily; can drop to 20 micrograms with a potent antiovulatory progestin

cards.q: Phased (triphasic) pill principle
cards.a: Estrogen constant (30-40 micrograms), progestin rises in phases to mimic cycle

cards.q: Who is favoured for phased pills
cards.a: Women over 35 years, or with breakthrough or no withdrawal bleeding on monophasic pill

cards.q: Progestin-only pill (minipill) rationale
cards.a: Removes estrogen; daily, continuous, no gap

cards.q: Ovulation rate on progestin-only pill
cards.a: About 20-30% of women ovulate

cards.q: Standard emergency (postcoital) regimen
cards.a: Levonorgestrel 0.75 mg two doses 12 hours apart, or 1.5 mg single dose

cards.q: Emergency regimen time limit
cards.a: Within 72 hours of unprotected intercourse

cards.q: Older emergency method (Yuzpe) components
cards.a: Levonorgestrel 0.5 mg plus ethinylestradiol 0.1 mg, two doses

cards.q: Antiprogestin used for emergency contraception in Europe and China
cards.a: Mifepristone 600 mg within 72 hours

cards.q: When emergency contraception should be used
cards.a: Only for unexpected exposure (rape, condom rupture)

cards.q: Depot medroxyprogesterone acetate dose and interval
cards.a: 150 mg i.m. every 3 months

cards.q: DMPA kinetics
cards.a: Peak in about 3 weeks; half-life about 50 days

cards.q: Norethindrone enanthate injectable dose and interval
cards.a: 200 mg i.m. every 2 months

cards.q: Main drawback of injectable progestin contraceptives
cards.a: Disrupted bleeding or amenorrhoea (more common with DMPA)

cards.q: Groups unsuited to DMPA (listed)
cards.a: Adolescent girls and lactating mothers

cards.q: Injectable combined estrogen-progestin preparations in India
cards.a: Not allowed (discontinued in most countries)

cards.q: Norplant system and capsule content
cards.a: Six capsules, each containing 36 mg levonorgestrel; release over 1-5 years

cards.q: Removal requirement for implants
cards.a: Non-biodegradable rubber implants must be removed; biodegradable polymer need not be

cards.q: Progesterone-releasing intrauterine insert and content
cards.a: Levonorgestrel 52 mg; works 5 years; acts mainly locally

cards.q: Transdermal contraceptive patch components and regimen
cards.a: Norelgestromin plus ethinylestradiol; weekly for 3 weeks, then 1 week off

cards.q: Hormonal contraceptive mechanism 1
cards.a: Pituitary feedback: progestin slows LH pulses; estrogen suppresses FSH

cards.q: Hormonal contraceptive mechanism 2
cards.a: Hostile cervical mucus against sperm (except postcoital pill)

cards.q: Hormonal contraceptive mechanism 3
cards.a: Endometrium out of phase, preventing implantation

cards.q: Fertility return after stopping oral contraceptives
cards.a: Within 1-2 months; rebound fertility; multiple pregnancy chance if conception in 2-3 cycles

cards.q: Fertility return after injectables
cards.a: Delayed; cycles may take months to normalise

cards.q: Management of breakthrough bleeding on pills
cards.a: Switch to a pill with higher estrogen dose (50 micrograms ethinylestradiol)

cards.q: Combined pill failure rate on perfect use
Non-serious adverse effects of contraceptives
cards.a: Nausea, headache, breakthrough bleeding (early cycles)

cards.q: Later androgenic adverse effects of 19-nortestosterone progestins
cards.a: Weight gain, acne, increased body hair (desogestrel relatively free)

cards.q: Pigmentation adverse effect of oral contraceptives
cards.a: Chloasma (cheeks, nose, forehead)

cards.q: Serious thromboembolic risk with low-dose pills
cards.a: About 2-3 per 1000 women-years; higher over 35, diabetics, hypertensives

cards.q: Mechanisms of OC thrombosis (listed)
cards.a: Raised clotting factors, decreased antithrombin III, decreased endothelial plasminogen activator, platelet aggregation

cards.q: Blood pressure effect of older pills
cards.a: Rise in 5-10% of women; stop pill, BP normalises in 3-6 months

cards.q: OC effect on lipids and HDL
cards.a: Estrogen raises HDL:LDL; progestin cancels benefit; low-dose pills no significant change

cards.q: Protective effect of OCs against endometrial cancer
cards.a: Shown for the progestin component

cards.q: Benign liver tumour linked to OCs
cards.a: Hepatoma (may rupture or turn malignant); slightly higher incidence

cards.q: Absolute contraindications to combined pill (list first items)
cards.a: Thromboembolic, coronary or cerebrovascular disease; moderate-severe hypertension; hyperlipidaemia; active liver disease

cards.q: Stop pill before major surgery
cards.a: 4 weeks before surgery

cards.q: Relative contraindications to combined pill: list all
cards.a: Diabetes, obesity, smoking, undiagnosed vaginal bleeding, uterine leiomyoma, mental illness, age over 35, mild hypertension, migraine, gallbladder disease

cards.q: Enzyme inducers that reduce pill efficacy (listed)
cards.a: Phenytoin, phenobarbitone, primidone, carbamazepine, rifampin, ritonavir

cards.q: Antibiotics that reduce pill efficacy by suppressing gut flora
cards.a: Tetracyclines, ampicillin

cards.q: Rifampin advice with contraception
cards.a: Use an alternative contraceptive method

cards.q: Non-contraceptive benefits of OCs (listed)
cards.a: Lower endometrial and ovarian cancer risk; less menstrual blood loss; fewer dysmenorrhoea, endometriosis and PID symptoms

cards.q: Ormeloxifene class and origin
cards.a: Nonsteroidal SERM developed at CDRI, India, as an oral contraceptive

cards.q: Ormeloxifene mechanism in endometrium
cards.a: Estrogen antagonist; suppresses endometrial proliferation by down-regulating ER

cards.q: Ormeloxifene half-life and contraceptive dose
cards.a: About 1 week; 30 mg twice weekly for 12 weeks, then weekly

cards.q: Ormeloxifene use in dysfunctional uterine bleeding
cards.a: 60 mg twice weekly for 12 weeks, then weekly for 12 weeks

cards.q: Why male contraception is hard (listed)
cards.a: Millions of sperm per ejaculate; spermatogenesis takes 64 days; testosterone loss causes impotence

cards.q: Gossypol source and effect
cards.a: Cottonseed compound; suppresses spermatogenesis; about 10% men stay oligozoospermic

cards.q: Chief adverse effect of gossypol
cards.a: Hypokalaemia with muscle weakness or paralysis; use has been dropped

cards.q: Male contraceptive approaches with the unacceptable side effect of feminisation
cards.a: Estrogens and progestins (gonadotropin suppression)

cards.q: Male contraceptive toxic agents named
cards.a: Cadmium, nitrofurans, indoles

cards.q: Male contraceptive approaches tried, named in chapter: list
cards.a: Antiandrogens, estrogens and progestins, androgens, superactive GnRH analogues, cytotoxic agents, gossypol

cards.q: Injectable contraceptives named: list
cards.a: Depot medroxyprogesterone acetate (DMPA), norethindrone enanthate (NEE)

cards.q: Implant and intrauterine progestin systems named: list
cards.a: Norplant (levonorgestrel implants), progesterone-releasing levonorgestrel intrauterine insert

cards.q: Hormone secreted with vasopressin by the posterior pituitary, and its main action
cards.a: Oxytocin: increases force and frequency of uterine contraction

cards.q: Who separated oxytocin from vasopressin, and when
cards.a: du Vigneaud, 1953

cards.q: Carrier protein that stores oxytocin in neurohypophysis
cards.a: Neurophysin

cards.q: Oxytocin receptor type on myometrium
cards.a: G-protein coupled; acts via Ca2+ influx and IP3 mediated release

cards.q: Uterine sensitivity to oxytocin in pregnancy
cards.a: Low early in pregnancy; highest at term; estrogens increase receptors

cards.q: Segment of uterus contracted by oxytocin at term
cards.a: Fundus and body; lower segment is not contracted

cards.q: Oxytocin action on breast
cards.a: Contracts myoepithelium, forcing milk out (milk ejection reflex)

cards.q: Oxytocin cardiovascular effect at high dose
cards.a: Vasodilatation, brief fall in BP, reflex tachycardia

cards.q: Oxytocin renal effect at high dose
cards.a: ADH-like: reduced urine output; pulmonary oedema with large i.v. fluid volumes

cards.q: Whether oxytocin is obligatory for labour
cards.a: Not obligatory (delivery occurs without it); facilitatory role

cards.q: Oxytocin route and plasma half-life
cards.a: i.v. or i.m. (not oral); half-life 6-12 minutes, shorter at term

cards.q: Enzyme in pregnant uterus and placenta that degrades oxytocin
cards.a: Oxytocinase

cards.q: Oxytocin potency conversion
cards.a: 1 IU equals 2 micrograms of pure hormone

cards.q: Oxytocin infusion for labour induction (dilution)
cards.a: 5 IU in 500 mL glucose or saline (10 mIU/mL), started slowly

cards.q: Why oxytocin is preferred over ergometrine or PGs for induction and augmentation
cards.a: Short half-life controls action; allows relaxation between contractions; spares lower segment

cards.q: Oxytocin dose for postpartum haemorrhage and caesarean
cards.a: KDT: 5 IU i.m. or by i.v. infusion; GG14: 10 units i.m. after delivery

cards.q: Oxytocin use in breast engorgement
cards.a: Only when milk ejection is inefficient; does not increase milk production

cards.q: Oxytocin challenge test purpose
cards.a: Assesses uteroplacental adequacy in high-risk pregnancy; rarely done

cards.q: Serious adverse effects of oxytocin (two)
cards.a: Uterine rupture and fetal asphyxia (injudicious use); water intoxication with large doses

cards.q: Buccal oxytocin analogue and tablet strength
cards.a: Desamino-oxytocin (Buctocin) 50 IU tablet

cards.q: Long-acting oxytocin analogue for PPH and caesarean atony
cards.a: Carbetocin

cards.q: Ergot alkaloids used in obstetrics
cards.a: Only the amine alkaloids: ergometrine and methylergometrine

cards.q: Ergometrine effect on uterus
cards.a: Increases force, frequency and duration; high doses cause tonic contracture

cards.q: Methylergometrine compared with ergometrine
cards.a: More potent on uterus; other actions less marked; has replaced ergometrine in many units

cards.q: Onset of ergometrine action by oral route
cards.a: About 15 minutes (i.m. 5 minutes; i.v. almost immediate)

cards.q: Ergometrine half-life and duration of single dose
cards.a: Half-life 1-2 hours; effect lasts 3-4 hours

cards.q: Ergometrine effect on lactation with prolonged high-dose use
cards.a: Reduces milk secretion via prolactin inhibition (dopaminergic)

cards.q: Ergometrine contraindications (listed)
cards.a: Pregnancy and before third stage of labour; hypertension or toxaemia; sepsis (gangrene); liver and kidney disease

cards.q: Ergometrine dose to prevent postpartum haemorrhage
cards.a: 0.2-0.3 mg i.m. at delivery of anterior shoulder (selected patients only)

cards.q: Ergometrine dose for active PPH
cards.a: 0.5 mg i.v.; combined with oxytocin 5 IU for severe bleeding

cards.q: Use of ergometrine or methylergometrine after caesarean or instrumental delivery
cards.a: 0.125 mg three times daily orally for 7 days (multiparae)

cards.q: Diagnostic use of ergometrine
cards.a: Small i.v. dose during angiography to provoke variant angina spasm

cards.q: Prostaglandins most potent as uterine stimulants
cards.a: PGE2, PGF2 alpha and 15-methyl PGF2 alpha (late pregnancy)

cards.q: Prostaglandin analogue used obstetrically with fewer side effects
cards.a: Misoprostol

cards.q: Extra-amniotic agent for second-trimester termination
cards.a: Ethacridine (150 mg in 150 mL infusion)

cards.q: Beta-2 agonist approved to suppress premature labour (still in UK and India)
cards.a: Ritodrine; i.v. infusion started at 50 micrograms/min

cards.q: Ritodrine treatment duration limit
cards.a: Not beyond 48 hours

cards.q: Serious maternal effects of ritodrine (listed)
cards.a: Hypotension, tachycardia, arrhythmia, pulmonary oedema, hyperglycaemia, hypokalaemia

cards.q: Contraindications to ritodrine (listed)
cards.a: Diabetes, heart disease, beta-blocker or steroid therapy

cards.q: Other beta-2 agonists used as tocolytic alternatives
cards.a: Salbutamol and terbutaline

cards.q: Calcium channel blocker used as tocolytic
cards.a: Nifedipine (early use can postpone labour)

cards.q: Oxytocin receptor antagonist tocolytic
cards.a: Atosiban; approved in Europe and UK for 24-33 weeks, not in USA or India

cards.q: Magnesium sulfate use in obstetrics
cards.a: First line for seizures in pre-eclampsia and eclampsia; tocolysis risky

cards.q: Tocolytic mechanism of magnesium sulfate
cards.a: Competes with Ca2+ entry through voltage and ligand-gated channels

cards.q: Progesterone use against preterm labour
cards.a: High-dose progesterone in later pregnancy for high-risk women (some success in trials)

cards.q: Halothane use in obstetrics
cards.a: Uterine relaxant; used during external or internal version

cards.q: Indomethacin (COX inhibitor) as a tocolytic
cards.a: Used off-label (GG14); avoid beyond 32 weeks (ductus closure); courses under 72 hours safer

cards.q: Uterine stimulants (oxytocics) named in the chapter: list
cards.a: Oxytocin, carbetocin, desamino-oxytocin, ergometrine, methylergometrine, PGE2, PGF2 alpha, misoprostol

cards.q: Tocolytic drugs named in the chapter: list
cards.a: Ritodrine, salbutamol, terbutaline, isoxsuprine, nifedipine, atosiban, magnesium sulfate, progesterone, indomethacin

cards.q: 5-alpha reductase inhibitors named in the chapter: list
cards.a: Finasteride, dutasteride

cards.q: Intracavernosal and urethral non-PDE5 agents named: list
cards.a: Papaverine, phentolamine, alprostadil (PGE1), MUSE urethral pellet

cards.q: Estrogens named in the chapter: list
cards.a: Estradiol, estrone, estriol, ethinylestradiol, mestranol, conjugated estrogens, estriol succinate, diethylstilbestrol, fosfestrol, dienestrol

cards.q: Injectable estradiol esters named in the chapter: list
